payload.name: Enumerate additional favorites after partial retrieval
payload.description: When a question asks for a plural list of a person's favorite or liked items and the first search returns some concrete items, run a supplementary preference-term search and aggregate all named candidates before answering.
content: If the question asks for a plural list of a person's favorite/liked items and the first search returns some concrete items, do not answer immediately; run an additional search combining the person's name with preference terms (favorite, likes, prefers, enjoys) and the item category, without restricting memory_kind.

Inspect event-kind memories whose predicate is 'preference' and activity memories where the person made, enjoyed, or suggested an item; if they name a distinct category item, treat it as a candidate favorite and include it in the enumeration.

Before finalizing, aggregate all distinct candidate items from the retrieved memories; include a retrieved item if it fits the category and appears in a favorable context for the person, even if the memory lacks the word 'favorite'.

solves: Solves plural favorite/like enumerations where initial retrieval returns some items but misses other favorites stored as event-kind preference predicates or activity memories. The diagnosed cause was stopping after the strongest memories instead of re-searching preference terms and aggregating all named candidates. Applies to any topic (desserts, books, foods); not to single-item, yes/no, or non-preference facts.
